# Allow list of invented account and card identifiers used in this repository.
#
# gate:privacy fails on any account-number or card-number shape anywhere in
# the tree that is not listed here. That is the point. The check is not "is
# there an identifier", because fixtures need identifiers, it is "is this one
# known". A new one stops the gate until a person looks at where it came from.
#
# Nothing on this list may be taken from a real statement. When adding an
# entry, say where you invented it. If you cannot say, it does not go on the
# list.
#
# HOW MATCHING WORKS. Once a value is FOUND, both sides are normalised the
# same way before comparison: spaces and dashes are removed, mask glyphs are
# folded so x and X and * are one value, and letters are upper-cased.
#
# WHAT IS FOUND is three separate patterns, and they do not cover the same
# ground. Stated one by one because this paragraph has now been wrong in
# both directions (fix round 4 finding CR3-M3P3-02, fix round 5 findings
# HZ4-M3P3-02 and CR4-M3P3-01): first it under-promised, then it replaced
# that with "case-insensitively and accept letters in the body", which is
# true of one pattern each and of neither on its own.
#
#   LOCAL account shape: two letters, two digits, then twelve DIGITS in
#   groups of four, separated by spaces or not. Either case. This is the
#   Belgian-length shape and it is the only one that tolerates separators.
#
#   FOREIGN account shape: two letters, two digits, then ten to thirty
#   letters-or-digits, COMPACT only, either case. This is what reaches an
#   account number whose body carries letters. It takes no separators on
#   purpose: allowing them inside a variable-length body made the match run
#   past the account number into the following word and invented shapes
#   nobody could write a provenance note for, measured in fix round 4.
#
#   CARD shapes: sixteen digits in four groups, and the masked form, both
#   with separators and either case.
#
# SO WHAT NEITHER ACCOUNT PATTERN COVERS, said plainly: an account number
# whose body carries letters AND is written with spaces or hyphens is found
# by nothing here. The local pattern refuses the letters and the foreign one
# refuses the separators. Nothing in the tree is written that way today and
# every value that is, is listed; a future fixture that writes one would go
# unchecked, and closing it means giving the foreign shape a separator rule
# that cannot run past the value.
#
# Binary and lockfile paths are skipped, because grep reads no text in them;
# a committed PDF is scanned, and rule 3 of the script refuses a compressed
# one for that reason.

# --- accounts -------------------------------------------------------------

# The IBAN example from the Wikipedia IBAN article, and a digit-shuffled
# variant. The household's current account across the unit, property and e2e
# fixtures.
BE68539007547034

# counterparty account distinct from the current account.

# are real Belgian prefixes, account bodies are the run 123456 continued.
BE71096123456769

# Transfer counterparty in the pairing and merchant tests.
BE02979245566602

# test/fixtures/generate-pdf-fixtures.ts. Bodies are sequential runs.
BE90012345678944

# Accounts in the original design prototype at
# design/reference/pulse-prototype.html. Constructed by typing a BE, two
# check digits and twelve digits by hand until the shape read like an
# account number; neither validates under the IBAN mod-97 check, which is
# positive evidence they were made up rather than copied. Provenance note
# added in fix round 2 (finding CR-M3P3-06): the note here used to say
# where they are USED, and this file's own rule at the top asks where they
# were INVENTED, which is the one thing it did not say.
BE71479602578213
BE68973942180011

# Documented placeholder. Deliberately not a valid IBAN: check digits 00
# never validate. Used in the mobile mockup under delivery/design/.
BE00000000000000

# --- accounts whose body carries letters -----------------------------------
# Surfaced in fix round 4 (finding HZ3-M3P3-03) when the account pattern was
# widened to accept letters in the body: until then no pattern here matched a
# non-Belgian account number at all, and these had been sitting in tracked
# fixtures with the gate exiting 0.
#
# All three are the PUBLISHED WORKED EXAMPLES from the IBAN specification's
# own documentation, the same source the first entry in this file names, used
# by the generic delimited fixtures to exercise a non-Belgian counterparty
# column. None was transcribed from anything: each was copied from public
# specification text, and each was probed against every real statement in the
# container and returns zero hits.
DE89370400440532013000
FR1420041010050500013M02606
NL91ABNA0417164300

# --- card numbers ---------------------------------------------------------
# Present so the masking work in M3-P6 has something to mask. None is a live
# PAN: each is a test prefix or a visible pattern.

# The 4000 test-card prefix continued with the run 123456789010, in the M3-P6
# masking fixtures and work history.
4000123456789010
4000-1234-5678-9010

# Straight digit runs, used where the fixture only needs a card shape.
1234567890123456
9999999999999999

# Patterned invented PANs in the Belfius PDF fixtures and the M3-P6 notes.
5599208877665544
5390754170349210

# Masked forms of the two invented PANs above. A card statement prints only
# the masked form, so the gate must know these as well as the bare digits.
400012XXXXXX9010
559920XXXXXX5544

# The two cards of the KBC PDF fixtures, in the masked form a card
# statement prints (test/fixtures/generate-pdf-fixtures.ts and the KBC
# fixture PDFs built from it). Invented the same way as the patterned PANs
# above: a Mastercard-shaped six-digit head, the mask glyphs the layout
# itself prints, and a hand-picked four-digit tail, one descending and one
# ascending so the pair reads as made up at a glance. The second exists so
# a fixture can carry a SECOND card of the same issuer, which is what the
# two-cards-one-account finding needed to be witnessed.
#
# Checked before listing, not asserted: each was probed against every real
# statement present in the container at fix-round-2 review time, in its
# masked form, its six-digit head and its four-digit tail, and returned
# zero WHOLE-TOKEN hits in all three forms in both documents. QUALIFIED IN
# FIX ROUND 4 (finding CR3-M3P3-03), because the unqualified sentence was
# true under a token reading and false under a plain one: a four-digit tail
# is four digits, and four digits turn up inside longer unrelated reference
# runs. What was checked, and what matters, is that no probe occurs as a
# value in its own right. That is the only check available to anyone here,
# and it is the one that would have caught a transcription.
541788XXXXXX3210
541788XXXXXX7654

# The third card, added in fix round 3 for the credit-balance statement
# fixture, so that family keeps one card per document and the identity
# witnesses stay unambiguous. Invented and probed the same way as the two
# above: masked form, six-digit head and four-digit tail, zero hits in all
# three forms against every real statement in the container.
541788XXXXXX9081

# The fourth card, added in fix round 4 for the underpaid statement
# fixture. Same construction and the same three-form check as the three
# above.
541788XXXXXX6503

# --- accounts invented by M3-P14, valid under the platform check ----------
# M3-P14 turns the ISO 7064 mod-97 check into a REFUSAL at the registration
# form (criterion 14.12), and criteria 14.1, 14.5, 14.16 and 15.1 require
# accounts to be registered through that form. A re-measurement of this tree
# at the phase base, by the method M3-P14 step 1 baseline FOUR records (git
# ls-files with the privacy gate's skip list, that gate's IBAN alternation in
# both arms, that gate's normalisation, then ISO 7064), found 17 distinct
# account-shaped values of which 7 pass and 10 fail. So the accounts those
# criteria register are invented here rather than borrowed from above.
#
# HOW EACH WAS INVENTED, so the rule at the top of this file is answered: a
# BE country code; a three-digit bank prefix taken from the 90x range, which
# no Belgian bank uses, grouped by purpose (901 pot, 902 reserve, 903 the
# ring-correction arms); a seven-digit body counting up in a visible pattern;
# the two-digit Belgian national check computed from those ten digits; and
# the two IBAN check digits computed by src/platform/account-number.ts so
# each number passes the very check the form now enforces. Nothing was
# transcribed. Each was probed against every real statement present in the
# container and returns zero hits.

# The account-registry fixture's own current account and its three pot siblings.
BE90901100001132
BE66901100002243
BE42901100003354
BE18901100004465

# Its four reserve-ring siblings.
BE24902200001138
BE97902200002249
BE73902200003360
BE49902200004471

# THE 903 GROUP, ONE LINE PER NUMBER WITH ITS OWN ROLE.
#
# CORRECTED IN PLACE AND LOUDLY (clause R-087), NOT QUIETLY REWRITTEN. These
# four numbers used to share ONE gloss naming FOUR roles with no mapping from
# gloss to number: "the savings account of the held-rows and declaration
# arms, the ordinary current account of the ring-correction arm that moves
# the spend total, a spare outside counterparty, and a second current
# account". A reader could not tell which number was which, so
# BE07903300003366 was simultaneously "a spare outside counterparty" and "a
# second current account", and the fixture row using it carried a descriptor
# reading OWN ACCOUNT SECOND. Criterion 14.15 witness SEVEN's third shape is
# a payment made to someone the household does NOT own, so that ambiguity was
# an invitation for a later phase to register the number as a household
# account and quietly turn the payment out into a second movement between two
# of the household's own accounts. The gloss is kept above rather than
# deleted so the next reader can see it changed.
#
# THE GLOSS WAS ALSO WRONG ABOUT THREE OF THE FOUR, which is why the split is
# a re-measurement and not a re-wording. Measured at this head with
# `grep -rn <number> .` over the whole tree excluding .git and node_modules:
# only BE07903300003366 appears in any fixture. The other three appear in no
# fixture at all, only in the validity list at
# test/domain/account-number.test.ts, so the roles the gloss assigned them
# are roles nothing fills today.
#
# All four were invented the same way as the 901 and 902 groups above: BE, a
# three-digit bank prefix from the 90x range no Belgian bank uses, a
# seven-digit body counting up in a visible pattern, the two-digit Belgian
# national check computed from those ten digits, and the two IBAN check
# digits computed by src/platform/account-number.ts. Nothing was transcribed.

# RESERVED, and used by nothing at this head. Invented for a savings account
# in the held-rows and declaration arms; those arms use the 902 group
# instead, so this number is on the list only because the validity test names
# it.
BE55903300001144

# RESERVED, and used by nothing at this head. Invented for the ordinary
# current account of the ring-correction arm; that arm uses the 901 group
# instead.
BE31903300002255

# AN OUTSIDE COUNTERPARTY, AND NOT AN ACCOUNT OF ANY HOUSEHOLD IN ANY
# FIXTURE. It is the payee of the payment made straight out of savings in
# test/fixtures/ar-savings.csv, the file's one NEGATIVE row whose
# counterparty the household does not own, which is one of the three rows
# criterion 14.15 witness SEVEN pins. That witness's shape for it is "a
# NEGATIVE row whose counterpartyIban belongs to no account of this
# household", so the moment any fixture or any test declares this number as a
# household account the row stops being a payment out and the witness stops
# witnessing what it exists for.
#
# THAT IS ASSERTED AND NOT ONLY STATED. A fast-gate test in
# test/domain/account-number.test.ts walks every committed CSV fixture, reads
# each one's OWN-ACCOUNT column through the shipped profile detector and
# parser, and requires this number to appear in no file's own-account list;
# and it walks the test tree for every textual occurrence of the number and
# requires each one to sit on a declared allow list, so a registration
# written anywhere reddens.
BE07903300003366

# RESERVED, and used by nothing at this head. Invented for a second current
# account; no fixture carries one.
BE80903300004477

# THE SECOND RESERVE ACCOUNT OF THE SAVINGS STATEMENT, added by criterion
# 14.15 witness SEVEN. That witness pins the three rows a reserve statement
# is the only source of, and one of them is a movement between TWO of the
# household's own reserve accounts, which needs the household to hold a
# second one. It is the counterparty of the third row of
# test/fixtures/ar-savings.csv.
#
# HOW IT WAS INVENTED, on the same terms as the block above and continuing
# the same visible run: a BE country code; the reserve group's 902 bank
# prefix, which is in the 90x range no Belgian bank uses; the seven-digit
# body 2000055, which continues the run 2000011, 2000022, 2000033, 2000044
# of the four reserve siblings above; the Belgian two-digit national check
# 82 computed from those ten digits, continuing that run's 38, 49, 60, 71;
# and the two IBAN check digits computed by src/platform/account-number.ts,
# so it passes the very ISO 7064 check criterion 14.12 turns into a refusal
# at the registration form. Nothing was transcribed. It was probed against
# every real statement present in the container and returns zero hits.
#
# ITS VALIDITY IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN CLAIMED HERE: a fast-gate unit test
# in test/domain/account-number.test.ts runs it through the shipped
# verifyAccountNumber, because the measurement this phase re-ran at its own
# base found 7 of 17 committed account-shaped values passing that check and
# a provenance note is not a test.
BE25902200005582

# --- deliberately INVALID shapes, for the four refusals -------------------
# Criterion 14.12 turns the platform validity test into a refusal at the
# registration form, and the four refusals need four inputs that fail in four
# different ways. Each is derived from BE90901100001132 above by one visible
# mutation, so the provenance of every one of them is "the invented number on
# the line above, damaged on purpose":
#   country letters replaced by a pair the pinned table does not carry;
#   one digit removed, so the length disagrees with the table;
#   the last two digits transposed, which is the mistyping the check exists
#   for; and one digit changed, which is the other one.
# The gate finds SHAPES, not valid account numbers, so a deliberately broken
# shape needs listing exactly like a working one.
ZZ90901100001132
BE9090110000113
BE90901100001123
BE90901100001133

# The transposed pair, for the browser half of the refusal (criterion 14.12).
# BE24902200001138 above with its last two digits swapped, so the mod-97
# check fails on exactly the mistyping the check exists for: a household
# typing sixteen characters from a paper statement on a phone.
BE24902200001183
